one_liner: Bit-packed Bernoulli sampler (AND/NOT of random bits, AVX2, optional LLVM JIT) versus std::bernoulli_distribution over mt19937_64.
what_it_does: Fills a 32-byte-aligned buffer with Bernoulli(p) bits packed 256 to a block, instead of returning one bool per std::bernoulli_distribution call. CreateSampler(p, tol) returns a TSamplerPtr functor that takes a std::mt19937_64 and a buffer from MakeBuffer(nobits); Expand() turns the packed bits into a vector<bool> or vector<T>. A Cython module exposes sample(prob, nobits, tol, seed, ise, jit, std), which returns one uint8 per bit.
how_it_is_fast: Quantize() binary-searches p into a short program of AND and NOT operations on uniform random words (ANDing two independent Bernoulli(1/2) bits halves p, NOT gives 1 - p), so each output bit costs a few raw PRNG bits and no float compare or branch; at p = 0.6 and tol 1e-3 it is 16 ops over 11 source words. The executor applies the program to whole 256-bit ymm registers (TAvxExecutor) or 64-bit words (TGeneralExecutor), in place over a buffer pre-filled with mt19937_64 output. The LLVM JIT (ORC LLJIT, LLVM 8 or 9) emits a straight-line function per plan, which removes the per-op switch but is still called once per 32-byte block through a function pointer.
when_to_use: Bulk fixed-p Bernoulli masks of thousands to millions of bits (random graph adjacency bits, dropout or erasure masks, coding-theory channel simulation) where the consumer reads packed bits.
Throughput-bound code on x86-64 with AVX2 where about 1e-3 absolute error in p is acceptable.
Moderate p (roughly 0.05 to 0.95), where the absolute tolerance is small relative to p.
As a reference for the AND/NOT bit-combination trick to re-implement in your own code base (the core executor plus Quantize is under 150 lines, BSD-3-Clause).
when_not_to_use: You need the exact p or a small p: the tolerance is absolute, so p = 1e-4 at the default 1e-3 yields 2^-11 (about 4.9e-4, 4.9x too high) and p = 1e-6 yields about 488x too high (derived by porting Quantize).

Non-x86 targets, MSVC, or CPUs with AVX but no AVX2 (Sandy and Ivy Bridge): the code includes <x86intrin.h>/<cpuid.h>, uses C++20-style designated initializers under C++17, and is built with -mavx2 throughout.

Entropy-efficient sampling: every output bit consumes NoSrcBlocks raw bits (11 at p = 0.6) against about 0.97 bits of entropy; issue #2's reporter moved to the Fast Loaded Dice Roller for that reason.
Small or per-call Python use: sample() builds a new sampler (and with jit=True a new LLVM JIT module) on every call, leaks its heap-allocated TRng, and expands the result to one byte per bit.
Projects that need a maintained dependency or modern LLVM: no commits since 2019-10-28, no releases, not on PyPI, and the JIT path has an #error for LLVM other than 8 or 9.

integration.dependencies: none for the AOT samplers; LLVM 8 or 9 for the JIT executor; Google Benchmark, GTest and Cython only for benchmarks, tests and the Python wheel
integration.min_toolchain: C++17 with GCC or Clang (designated initializers, <x86intrin.h>, <cpuid.h>), CMake 3.15
integration.platforms: x86-64 only; AVX2 required in practice (library compiled with -mavx -mavx2)
integration.thread_safety: README lists 'Thread-safe'; a sampler's plan is immutable after creation, so one sampler can be shared if each thread passes its own mt19937_64 and buffer (inferred from source, not documented further)

gotchas: TSamplerPtr::operator() returns bool converted from EStatus, and EOk is 0, so it returns false on success; Validate() only checks 16-byte alignment while the AVX path uses aligned 32-byte loads, and the buffer must be NoSrcBlocks times the output size (11x at p = 0.6) with only its first 1/NoSrcBlocks holding samples. Use MakeBuffer() and ignore the return value's truthiness.

Auto dispatch checks only CPUID.1:ECX.AVX (no AVX2 or OSXSAVE check) but TAvxExecutor uses AVX2 integer ops, so it can fault with SIGILL on AVX-only CPUs; on non-AVX x86 Auto selects the unimplemented SSE executor and CreateSampler returns an empty pointer, as it also does when tol is too tight for 64 ops (below about 1e-13 for non-dyadic p). Calling an empty TSamplerPtr dereferences null.

Harness flaw behind the README table: it was produced at commit 13f57cc (2019-10-11), when TAvxExecutor applied the plan in reverse order (Ops_[NoOps_ - ip - 1]) while Quantize already reversed it; at p = 0.6 that build sampled about p = 0.40, not 0.6 (derived by porting Quantize). It was fixed in 0d005fd on 2019-10-18. The statistical test hard-codes Ise_ = General (still true at HEAD), so the AVX path was never checked for its mean. Timing is probably unaffected, since the op count is the same.

Other defects: the JIT emits add instead of or for EOp::Or (latent, since Quantize never emits Or); the std baseline ORs bits into an uninitialised buffer; BM_JitGenericSampler runs the non-JIT sampler; HEAD guards the JIT benchmarks with a misspelled USE_JIT_EXCUTOR; and the top-level CMakeLists checks a misspelled LLVM_VERION_MAJOR.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: No sibling in this category generates random variates; the closest in spirit are approximation kernels like SIMD-math-prims, which also trade exactness for SIMD throughput. Pick fast-bernoulli only for bulk packed Bernoulli bits on AVX2 x86, and treat it as an algorithm to vendor rather than a maintained library.
verified_claims_summary: Google Benchmark on an unnamed 4-core 3.4 GHz x86 with the compiler and flags unrecorded, p = 0.6, tol 1e-3, 128 blocks: per output bit, std::bernoulli_distribution over mt19937_64 took about 138 ns versus 3.18 ns (generic), 2.17 ns (AVX) and 1.70 ns (JIT AVX), i.e. about 43x, 64x and 81x (derived from page data). The README's raw 1000-1300x includes 16x more work for the std baseline. The same run's mt19937_64 call costs about 9.35 ns and a std::bernoulli_distribution draw needs one, so the 138 ns baseline is about 15x its own RNG floor, which points to an unoptimised build or a slow libstdc++ generate_canonical; the fast samplers are RNG-bound (5,632 mt19937_64 calls, about 52.6 us of JIT AVX's 55.7 us). Against a baseline running near its RNG floor the per-bit gain would be nearer 5-6x (64 versus 11 random bits per output bit; derived from page data).
status_note: Abandoned since 2019-10-28 (47 commits, 6 stars, no releases, not on PyPI), but BSD-3-Clause and small enough to vendor the Quantize and AVX executor; the JIT needs LLVM 8 or 9, and the README's AVX timings came from a build that sampled the wrong probability (fixed 2019-10-18).
